text:
Every Thursday at 3:12, Mara would find a book on the bread rack. Always the same: The Practical Guide to Inland Birds. Cracked blue spine, library stamp from a town forty miles away. She would put it on the flour bin, wipe butter off the cover, and mean to take it back after her shift. By noon, the errands, the heat, sleep, would swallow it.
Then next Thursday there it was, tucked in between the cooling rye loaves. Tonight the bakery hummed with the proofing cabinet and the old radio’s static. Rain pressed silver lines down the front window. She lifted the book with both hands as if it might be warm. A folded receipt marked the chapter on herons. She opened it. In block letters, someone had written: I THINK YOU ARE THE ONLY PERSON AWAKE WHEN I AM. Page 47.
She turned to page 47. A grey heron stood in a marsh, one foot raised, patient as a saint. Under the picture, in pencil: THURSDAY, 3:30?
The clock over the mixer clicked once.
Mara brushed flour from her apron, unlocked the front door, and turned on the little OPEN sign.
